alignments.note: Cleft frame *It is*: rule 20 marks such an impersonal *it* added, and the copula beside it answers to no predicate morpheme either, the clause's predication being carried by the finite verb יֶחְכָּמוּ.
Anarthrous substantival adjective takes the bare *the* the ASV supplies to make it a noun phrase, headed on the lexeme (rules 46, 31).

Corrected from the accepted reading, which folded this *that* into רַבִּים under rule 46. Rule 46 licenses a supplied relative only where it makes a clause or participle into a noun phrase; רַבִּים is a written antecedent already rendered *the great*, and this *that* subordinates the separate finite clause יֶחְכָּמוּ juxtaposed to it, which rule 46 excludes and rule 55 marks added. This is the treatment the chapter gives the supplied *which* at JOB.32.19, and it differs from JOB.32.12, where *that convinced* stands inside one participle's own rendering. The competing reading is the accepted one.
Finite verb with its copula, headed on the lexical predicate (rules 17, 24).
Waw fused with the gapped negation as *Nor*, aligned to the morpheme actually present (rule 35).
Anarthrous substantival adjective with its supplied bare *the*, headed on the lexeme (rules 46, 31).

The second cleft relative, added on the same terms as t006: זְקֵנִים is a written antecedent and יָבִינוּ a finite clause juxtaposed to it (rules 46, 55). The waw of this line is already spent on *Nor*, so it is not a home for a second connective either (rules 35, 51).

review_notes: Corrected: the two cleft relatives *that* (t006, t012) are `added` under rules 46 and 55 rather than part of the substantival adjectives' supplied noun phrases; the substantives keep the bare *the* rule 46 gives them.
*Nor* rests on a gapped negative in the second line and is aligned to the waw actually present, headed on it (rule 35).
The cleft frame *It is* remains a single added unit headed on the copula (rule 20).
